Management commands always use DjangoHelpFormatter, because `create_parser` hard-codes it as the default `formatter_class` in `kwargs.setdefault("formatter_class", DjangoHelpFormatter)`. `DjangoHelpFormatter` subclasses argparse's `HelpFormatter`. That class reflows the description text, which is why the newlines in your help string are lost. Passing a different `formatter_class` to `create_parser` overrides the default. AlterField.reduce in django/db/migrations/operations/fields.py now handles a following AlterField (as well as RemoveField) on the same field. It returns [operation], so consecutive AlterFields reduce to the last one even when other operations sit between them. The optimizer's `reduce` call on the left operation is what picks this up.

admin.E108 is raised in _check_list_display_item (django/contrib/admin/checks.py). The gap is the order of lookups: _meta.get_field(item) is tried first (line 913), so a reverse relation like "choice" is found and E108 is never raised; the getattr(obj.model, item) fallback only runs when get_field raises FieldDoesNotExist.

The code already handles this in `RenameIndex.reduce`. The optimizer uses it to collapse a chain of `RenameIndex` operations on the same model. When one operation's `new_name` matches the next one's `old_name`, it merges them into one `RenameIndex`. The merged operation keeps the first operation's `old_name` or `old_fields`. That is how a squashed index_together -> indexes transition can end up as a single `RenameIndex` with no deprecated index_together option left. I did not confirm that this method is the actual fix for the ticket, and I did not run a squash to check it. The related `AlterTogetherOptionOperation.can_reduce_through` at models.py:685 may also be part of the fix.

In Query._get_only_select_mask, line 792 uses field.remote_field.model to find the related model. For a reverse relation (a OneToOneRel) that resolves to the model the relation points back to, not the related model. The only() mask is therefore applied to the wrong model, and all fields of the related model are still selected. The fix is to use field.related_model for reverse relations, which is already handled by the `field in opts.related_objects` branch above it.
